messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game inspired by Fortnite Chapter 4 Season 1.

## Requirements
- User requested “everything” from Chapter 4 Season 1.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions; summarize assumptions when finishing.
- Build and verify the game, including a small JPEG screenshot for inspection.

## Decisions
- Created an original fan-made 2D battle royale named **Riftfall**, using original canvas-rendered art and avoiding official game assets.
- Implemented a solo match with 16 operators, Chapter 4 Season 1-inspired locations, loot, weapons, storm phases, and touch controls.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented the game in `index.html`, including a title screen, island rendering, POIs, AI opponents, weapons/combat, loot, storm circle, HUD/minimap, keyboard and touch controls, and victory/defeat screens.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully with `node --check`.
- Opened `http://localhost:3002` in Playwright and saved/inspected `screenshots/title.jpg`.

### Active
- Fix and verify the game after deployment; current UI screenshot was checked, but gameplay was not yet exercised.
- User’s broad “everything” request has not been fully met; this is a playable fan-made approximation.

### Blocked
- Browser console showed one error: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0` (non-game favicon request).

## Next Move
1. Exercise the match in Playwright: deploy, verify gameplay, inspect console errors, save and inspect a gameplay JPEG.
2. Fix any issues found, then summarize the fan-made approximation and controls to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire game implementation.
- `screenshots/title.jpg`: latest checked screenshot of the title screen.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright browser is open at `http://localhost:3002`; browser console only reported the favicon 404 so far.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game inspired by Fortnite Chapter 4 Season 1.
- Verify gameplay in-browser and save a small JPEG screenshot for inspection.

## Requirements
- User requested “everything” from Chapter 4 Season 1; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions and briefly state them when finishing.
- Build and verify the game, including a JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Create **Riftfall**, an original fan-made 2D battle royale with original canvas-rendered art and no official game assets.
- Include a solo match, 16 operators, themed locations, weapons, loot, storm phases, HUD/minimap, and keyboard/touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game in `index.html`, including title screen, island rendering, POIs, AI opponents, combat, loot, storm circle, HUD/minimap, controls, and victory/defeat screens.
- Saved and inspected `screenshots/title.jpg`.
- JavaScript syntax check passed for an extracted script copy before the latest browser test.

### Active
- Fix and verify the game after deployment; gameplay has not yet been successfully exercised.
- Finish the user’s request, which is currently a playable fan-made approximation rather than “everything” from the original season.

### Blocked
- Browser deployment test: clicking Deploy reports `ReferenceError: updateHud is not defined`. In `index.html`, the script closes at line 91 while `function updateHud()` appears after `</script></body></html>` at line 92, so it is outside the script.
- Browser console also reports `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.

## Next Move
1. Move `updateHud()` into the script before its closing tag, then reload and check browser console.
2. Exercise a match in Playwright: deploy, verify controls and gameplay, and inspect for runtime errors.
3. Save and inspect a gameplay JPEG, then summarize assumptions, controls, and verification.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire game implementation; contains the current `updateHud()` placement bug.
- `screenshots/title.jpg`: inspected title-screen screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright is open at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The previous `node --check` used `/tmp/opencode/game.js`, extracted before the latest gameplay test; re-extract and recheck after fixing script placement.
